title: Length of an append
description: Induction splits the goal into a nil case and a cons case; watch each one shrink to nothing.
source:
theorem len_append (xs ys : List Nat) : (xs ++ ys).length = xs.length + ys.length := by
  induction xs with
  | nil =>
    simp
  | cons x xs ih =>
    simp [ih]
    omega

steps.tactic: theorem len_append (xs ys : List Nat) : (xs ++ ys).length = xs.length + ys.length := by
steps.explanation: The statement to prove: appending two lists adds their lengths.
steps.raw:
xs ys : List Nat
⊢ (xs ++ ys).length = xs.length + ys.length

steps.explanation: Induction on xs. First case: xs is the empty list.
steps.raw:
case nil
ys : List Nat
⊢ ([] ++ ys).length = [].length + ys.length

steps.explanation: Both sides simplify to ys.length, so the nil case closes.
Second case: xs is x :: xs, and we get the induction hypothesis ih for the shorter list.
steps.raw:
case cons
ys : List Nat
x : Nat
xs : List Nat
ih : (xs ++ ys).length = xs.length + ys.length
⊢ (x :: xs ++ ys).length = (x :: xs).length + ys.length

steps.explanation: Simplifying with ih turns the goal into pure arithmetic about lengths.
steps.raw:
case cons
ys : List Nat
x : Nat
xs : List Nat
ih : (xs ++ ys).length = xs.length + ys.length
⊢ xs.length + ys.length + 1 = xs.length + 1 + ys.length

steps.explanation: omega solves the linear arithmetic. Both cases are closed: proof complete.
